source.title: A Practical Finite Element Modeling Strategy to Capture Cracking and Crushing Behavior of Reinforced Concrete Structures
source.rights_scope: The published article, including its figures, is CC BY 4.0 with attribution and change notice; no separate unpublished acquisition file or its rights have been identified.
source.data_availability_statement: The article says the data supporting its findings are contained within the article; it does not link an ordered numeric measurement file.
cited_locations: Section 2 and Figure 1, article pp. 3-4 (institutional PDF pp. 4-5): specimen, geometry, loading, sensors, and material table
Section 5.1 and Figure 19, article p. 20 (institutional PDF p. 21): measured load-versus-net-midspan-deflection plot and failure endpoint
Data Availability Statement, article p. 23 (institutional PDF p. 24)

specimen.identity: unstrengthened conventional-steel RC reference beam only
specimen.dominant_reported_mechanism: flexural failure after tensile steel yielding, governed by compression-zone concrete crushing
specimen.geometry_provenance: Figure 1 dimension transcription; the 1450 mm support-to-nose value follows symmetric 4200 and 1300 mm dimensions, not a surveyed station record.
reinforcement_from_figure_1: two top and two bottom nominal diameter 16 mm B500C steel bars
diameter 10 mm stirrups at 75 mm spacing
Figure 1 shows nominal side/top/bottom bar offsets; specimen-specific as-built bar coordinates are not published.
specimen.loading: two synchronized hydraulic jacks at the two noses, displacement controlled; Figure 1 labels each nose Load/2
specimen.supports: two movable steel roller supports described in Section 2; a model's horizontal rigid-body restraint and bearing compliance need an explicit convention
specimen.material_boundary: Table 1's concrete Ec=36.9 GPa, fc=51.1 MPa, and fct=3.6 MPa are code-estimated for C35/45 at 287 days; diameter-16 mm steel coupon Es=201 GPa and fy=510 MPa were experimentally measured. These are not a complete measured nonlinear material law.
specimen.observable_endpoint: Figure 19 plots experimental total load against net midspan deflection, derived from three LVDTs; Section 5.1 reports the test stopped at 65.0 kN and 79 mm when concrete crushing was observed.
specimen.pretest_condition: The authors attribute a weaker early cracking-stage response partly to shrinkage cracks and unexpected load during transport.

numeric_measurement_availability.published_observations: Figure 19 experimental plot and the reported 65.0 kN, 79 mm stopping endpoint

crosswalk_and_model_boundary.closer_mechanism_match_than_titanium_gro: The isolated reference has ordinary steel longitudinal bars and reported flexural crushing, without the companion beam's CFRP or the Zenodo 18735817 specimen's titanium/grout interface.
model_blockers: The public RC compiler on the main branch has a fully fixed serial-chain endpoint, not this two-bearing four-point setup; the experimental pin/roller path on PR 439 is not merged and is not the source's two-roller bearing description.
The source paper models steel-concrete bond slip and localized cracking, neither of which is established negligible for the current Euler-Bernoulli fiber element.
Concrete nonlinear properties are not all independently measured, and early shrinkage/transport damage is reported.
No ordered numeric load-deflection measurement file, published digitization uncertainty, or fixed-parameter held-out comparison is available in this intake.
